title: ETF Flow Persistence
market_niche: Liquid ETFs where allocation, model-portfolio, and risk-budget flows can move gradually across days or weeks.
phenomenon: ETF breakouts may persist when investor flows, allocation models, or risk controls keep buying the same asset after an initial move.
counterparty_or_forced_actor: Model-portfolio allocators, volatility-budgeted portfolios, benchmark-aware managers, ETF fund-flow followers, and slower retail-advisory reallocations.
why_edge_might_exist: Allocation flows often occur incrementally rather than instantly, so price pressure may continue after a clean breakout signal.
why_large_funds_might_ignore_it: The broad version is crowded and low edge; the smaller ETF version may have limited capacity, variable liquidity, operational monitoring overhead, and modest absolute P&L.

institutional_constraint_evidence.expected_daily_dollar_volume: high for broad ETFs and variable for narrower ETFs
institutional_constraint_evidence.estimated_position_size: unknown until ETF liquidity buckets are measured
institutional_constraint_evidence.estimated_strategy_capacity: likely moderate for personal capital, lower in niche ETFs after spread and impact assumptions
institutional_constraint_evidence.number_of_opportunities_per_year: depends on ETF universe breadth and breakout frequency

expected_capacity: Potentially useful for small personal capital, but capacity and edge quality must be measured by ETF liquidity bucket before treating it as deployable.
persistence_mechanism: Slow fund flows, staged reallocations, and risk-budget changes may continue after an ETF makes a new short-term high.
crowding_risk: Medium to high, because breakout continuation is well known and should be assumed fragile unless it survives costs, dates, and neighboring ETF universes.
edge_decay_trigger: The thesis weakens if breakout continuation only works in one date window, disappears after retail-liquid costs, or fails across multiple ETF groups.
observable_prediction: A prespecified ETF breakout rule should retain most buy-and-hold growth while reducing drawdown or improving risk-adjusted behavior in more than one ETF group.
falsification_tests: Reject the tested strategy hypothesis if return retention and drawdown improvement thresholds fail after realistic costs.
Weaken the thesis if the effect appears only in one symbol or one date window.
Treat the result as untested for deployment until liquidity and spread assumptions are reviewed by ETF group.
suggested_validation: Use a single prespecified breakout template before inspecting results.
Compare results across several ETF groups rather than repeatedly testing one symbol.
Require costs, date sensitivity, and train/test validation before strengthening the thesis.
references: Practitioner literature on ETF fund flows and allocation momentum
Academic literature on time-series momentum and flow-driven price pressure
